```{ojs}
import {withDownload, cellFeatures, fmt, locatorMap, placeMarks, boxPolygon} from "../assets/js/dl.js"
S = FileAttachment("data/mekong/summary.json").json()
B = FileAttachment("data/mekong/boundaries.json").json()
countries = FileAttachment("data/mekong/countries.geojson").json()
adm1 = FileAttachment("data/mekong/adm1.geojson").json()
adm2 = FileAttachment("data/mekong/adm2.geojson").json()
seasons = FileAttachment("data/mekong/seasons.csv").csv({typed: true})
cells = FileAttachment("data/mekong/cells.csv").csv({typed: true})
SEASON = ({dong_xuan: "Dong xuan (sown 1 Dec)", he_thu: "He thu (sown 20 Apr)"})
SEASON_COLOR = ({domain: Object.values(SEASON), range: ["#c98b2b", "#2b8a9b"]})
PERC = ({irrigated_perc1: 1, irrigated: 2, irrigated_perc4: 4})
bySeason = (rows, regime, season) => rows.filter(d => d.regime === regime && d.season === season)
mean = (rows, key) => d3.mean(rows, d => d[key])
```

| Setup | |
|---|---|
| Area | 105.2-106.2 E, 9.7-10.7 N, in the Mekong Delta (provinces below) |
| Crop map | MapSPAM 2020 rice, physical area [@spam2020] |
| Weather, soil | AgERA5 1990-2024 [@agera5]; SoilGrids 2.0 [@poggio2021], one profile per 0.1° cell |
| Crop, template | CERES-Rice, IR 64 (DSSAT cultivar IB0015), 105 kg N/ha; template `XDRW8601.RIX`, from the transplanted IRRI experiment IRMZ8601 (Muñoz, 1986) |
| Seasons | dong xuan transplanted on 1 December, he thu on 20 April, every year |
| Water | four regimes, each run on every rice cell: continuous flood (bund raised to 150 mm, flood kept at 5, then 30, then 50 mm) with percolation of 1, 2 (the experiment's own) or 4 mm a day; and rainfed behind the same bund |
| Years | 1991-2023, 33 dong xuan and 33 he thu seasons |
| Boundaries | edge-matched OCHA administrative boundaries (COD-AB) from HDX: [Viet Nam](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-vnm) (Government of Viet Nam), [Cambodia](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-khm), CC BY-IGO |
| Experiment file | [`configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/xdssat/blob/main/configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml) |

## Two seasons, two bills

A flooded rice field loses water every day: the crop transpires it, the sun evaporates it from the
water surface, and some of it seeps down through the puddled soil. To keep the flood, the farmer
pays the difference with irrigation. The model keeps the flood of the 1986 IRRI experiment and
counts every millimetre it has to add. One millimetre over a hectare is 10 cubic metres.

How fast water seeps through a puddled field is a property of the soil and of how it was puddled.
The experiment measured 2 mm a day; this case also runs half and double of that. The switch below sets
it for every chart on the page.

```{ojs}
viewof perc = Inputs.radio(new Map([["1 mm a day", "irrigated_perc1"], ["2 mm a day (the experiment)", "irrigated"],
  ["4 mm a day", "irrigated_perc4"]]), {value: "irrigated", label: "Percolation"})
```

```{ojs}
dx = bySeason(seasons, perc, "dong_xuan")
ht = bySeason(seasons, perc, "he_thu")
boxCells = cells.filter(d => d.regime === perc)
volume = s => d3.sum(boxCells.filter(d => d.season === s), d => d.IRCM * d.ha * 10) / 1e6
md`A dong xuan crop, grown through the dry months, takes **${fmt.int(mean(dx, "IRCM"))} mm** of irrigation in an average
year (${fmt.int(mean(dx, "IRCM") * 10)} m³ a hectare) and catches **${fmt.int(mean(dx, "PRCM"))} mm** of rain. A he thu
crop, sown as the rains begin, takes **${fmt.int(mean(ht, "IRCM"))} mm** and catches **${fmt.int(mean(ht, "PRCM"))} mm**.
If every rice hectare of the box grew both crops, the box would draw about **${fmt.int(volume("dong_xuan"))} million m³** of
irrigation water in the dry season and **${fmt.int(volume("he_thu"))} million m³** in the wet one, every year.`
```

```{ojs}
billRows = seasons.filter(d => d.regime === perc).map(d => ({...d, label: SEASON[d.season]}))
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 300, marginLeft: 55,
  x: {label: null, tickFormat: d => String(d), ticks: 8},
  y: {label: "Irrigation per season (mm)", grid: true, domain: [0, d3.max(seasons, d => d.IRCM) * 1.05]},
  color: {legend: true, ...SEASON_COLOR},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(billRows, {x: "season_year", y: "IRCM", stroke: "label", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.dot(billRows, {x: "season_year", y: "IRCM", fill: "label", r: 3, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.label}, ${d.season === "dong_xuan" ? `${d.season_year}-${d.season_year + 1}` : d.season_year + 1}\n` +
        `irrigation ${fmt.int(d.IRCM)} mm\nrain ${fmt.int(d.PRCM)} mm\nyield ${fmt.int(d.yield)} kg/ha`}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), "mekong_irrigation_by_year", "area-weighted mean of the rice cells; season year: the dong xuan crop of December, then the he thu crop of the next April")
```

## What the water buys

```{ojs}
gainOf = s => {
  const irr = bySeason(seasons, perc, s), rf = bySeason(seasons, "rainfed", s)
  const y = irr.map(d => ({year: d.season_year, irr: d.yield, rf: rf.find(e => e.season_year === d.season_year).yield, mm: d.IRCM}))
  return {rows: y, gain: d3.mean(y, d => d.irr - d.rf), mm: d3.mean(y, d => d.mm),
          rf: d3.mean(y, d => d.rf), irr: d3.mean(y, d => d.irr)}
}
gDx = gainOf("dong_xuan")
gHt = gainOf("he_thu")
md`The same fields, the same weather, the same rice, but only rain behind the bund: that is what the water has to beat.
In the dry season the flooded crop gives **${fmt.int(gDx.irr)} kg/ha** and the rainfed one **${fmt.int(gDx.rf)} kg/ha**:
${fmt.int(gDx.mm)} mm of irrigation buys **${fmt.int(gDx.gain)} kg** of grain, **${fmt.d2(gDx.gain / (gDx.mm * 10))} kg per m³**.
In the he thu season the rain does the work: flooded **${fmt.int(gHt.irr)}**, rainfed **${fmt.int(gHt.rf)} kg/ha**. The
${fmt.int(gHt.mm)} mm of irrigation the model adds to keep the flood ${Math.abs(gHt.gain) < 150 ? "buys almost nothing" :
gHt.gain > 0 ? `buys ${fmt.int(gHt.gain)} kg` : `comes with ${fmt.int(-gHt.gain)} kg less`}${gHt.gain < -150 ?
` (with the experiment's percolation, the rainfed crop matures a median 5 days later and takes up 199 rather than
188 kg N/ha)` : ""}. FAOSTAT puts Viet Nam's
national rice yield at 5.82-5.92 t/ha in 2018-2020 (<a href="#ref-faostat_qcl">FAO 2025</a>): the model's levels are higher, its differences are
the result.`
```

```{ojs}
buyRows = ["dong_xuan", "he_thu"].flatMap(s => gainOf(s).rows.flatMap(d => [
  {season: SEASON[s], year: d.year, water: "flooded", yield: d.irr, mm: d.mm},
  {season: SEASON[s], year: d.year, water: "rainfed", yield: d.rf, mm: 0}]))
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 300, marginLeft: 55,
  fx: {label: null},
  x: {label: null, tickFormat: d => String(d), ticks: 5},
  y: {label: "Grain yield (kg/ha)", grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["flooded", "rainfed"], range: ["#2b6cb0", "#c0392b"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.line(buyRows, {fx: "season", x: "year", y: "yield", stroke: "water", strokeWidth: 1.8}),
    Plot.dot(buyRows, {fx: "season", x: "year", y: "yield", fill: "water", r: 2.5, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.season}, season year ${d.year}\n${d.water}: ${fmt.int(d.yield)} kg/ha` +
        (d.mm ? `\nirrigation ${fmt.int(d.mm)} mm` : "")}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), "mekong_flooded_vs_rainfed", "area-weighted means; flooded at the chosen percolation")
```

## Where the water goes

```{ojs}
TERMS = [["EPCM", "taken up by the crop (transpiration)"], ["ESCM", "evaporated from soil and flood water"],
         ["DRCM", "drained below the roots"], ["ROCM", "ran off over the bund"], ["stored", "left in the field at harvest"]]
flow = ["irrigated_perc1", "irrigated", "irrigated_perc4", "rainfed"].flatMap(r => ["dong_xuan", "he_thu"].flatMap(s => {
  const rows = bySeason(seasons, r, s)
  const tag = r === "rainfed" ? "rainfed" : `flood, ${PERC[r]} mm/d`
  return TERMS.map(([k, name]) => ({regime: r, row: `${SEASON[s].split(" (")[0]}, ${tag}`, term: name,
    mm: Math.max(0, mean(rows, k)), inflow: mean(rows, "IRCM") + mean(rows, "PRCM")}))
}))
chosen = flow.filter(d => d.regime === perc)
cropShare = s => { const r = chosen.filter(d => d.row.startsWith(s)); return r[0].mm / r[0].inflow }
md`Every millimetre that enters a field (irrigation and rain) leaves it in one of four ways before the harvest, or
stays. With percolation at ${PERC[perc]} mm a day, the crop itself transpires **${fmt.pct(cropShare("Dong xuan"))}** of the
dry-season water and **${fmt.pct(cropShare("He thu"))}** of the wet-season water. The rest is the cost of keeping a field
flooded: evaporation from the water surface, seepage through the bottom of the field and, at harvest, a soaked soil
and a standing flood that the next season will not inherit in this model (each season starts afresh).`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 330, marginLeft: 150, marginRight: 20,
  x: {label: "Water per season (mm): irrigation and rain in, by where it goes", grid: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: [...new Set(flow.map(d => d.row))]},
  color: {legend: true, domain: TERMS.map(d => d[1]), range: ["#2f8f4e", "#e0a030", "#5b7fbf", "#8e7cc3", "#b0b0b0"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(flow, Plot.stackX({x: "mm", y: "row", fill: "term", order: TERMS.map(d => d[1]),
      fillOpacity: d => (d.regime === perc || d.regime === "rainfed" ? 1 : 0.35), tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.row}\n${d.term}: ${fmt.int(d.mm)} mm (${fmt.pct(d.mm / d.inflow)} of the water in)`})),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
}), "mekong_water_balance", "mean of 33 seasons, area-weighted; the chosen percolation in full colour; 'left in the field' = water in minus water out")
```

## The soil you cannot see

```{ojs}
pDx = p => mean(bySeason(seasons, p, "dong_xuan"), "IRCM")
pY = p => mean(bySeason(seasons, p, "dong_xuan"), "yield")
md`Percolation does not show in the harvest but it does in the bill. From 1 to 4 mm a day, a dong xuan crop's
irrigation goes from **${fmt.int(pDx("irrigated_perc1"))}** to **${fmt.int(pDx("irrigated_perc4"))} mm**, while its yield
moves from ${fmt.int(pY("irrigated_perc1"))} to ${fmt.int(pY("irrigated_perc4"))} kg/ha. The water that seeps away
leaves the bottom of the model's soil profile; where it goes from there is outside the model. The map shows how the
dry-season bill varies from cell to cell.`
```

```{ojs}
viewof mapMetric = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Irrigation", "IRCM"], ["Drained below the roots", "DRCM"],
  ["Grain bought per m³ of irrigation", "kgm3"]]), {value: "IRCM", label: "Dong xuan map"})
```

```{ojs}
dxCells = {
  const rf = new Map(cells.filter(d => d.regime === "rainfed" && d.season === "dong_xuan").map(d => [`${d.iy}_${d.ix}`, d.yield]))
  return cells.filter(d => d.regime === perc && d.season === "dong_xuan")
    .map(d => ({...d, rf: rf.get(`${d.iy}_${d.ix}`), kgm3: (d.yield - rf.get(`${d.iy}_${d.ix}`)) / (d.IRCM * 10)}))
}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 460, aspectRatio: 1,
  projection: {type: "equirectangular", domain: cellFeatures(dxCells)},
  color: {scheme: mapMetric === "kgm3" ? "Greens" : "Blues", legend: true,
          label: {IRCM: "Irrigation per dong xuan season (mm)", DRCM: "Drainage below the roots (mm)",
                  kgm3: "Grain bought per m³ of irrigation (kg)"}[mapMetric]},
  marks: [
    Plot.geo(cellFeatures(dxCells), {fill: d => d.properties[mapMetric], stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.4}),
    ...placeMarks(Plot, adm1, adm2, {labels: "adm1", fontSize: 9}),
    Plot.tip(dxCells, Plot.pointer({x: "lon", y: "lat",
      title: d => `${d.lat.toFixed(2)} N, ${d.lon.toFixed(2)} E\nirrigation ${fmt.int(d.IRCM)} mm, rain ${fmt.int(d.PRCM)} mm\n` +
        `drained ${fmt.int(d.DRCM)} mm\nflooded ${fmt.int(d.yield)} kg/ha, rainfed ${fmt.int(d.rf)} kg/ha\n` +
        `${fmt.d2(d.kgm3)} kg grain per m³\nrice ${fmt.int(d.ha)} ha`})),
    Plot.frame()
  ]
}), "mekong_dong_xuan_map", `dong xuan, mean of 33 seasons, percolation ${PERC[perc]} mm a day`)
```

## What this does not say

- **Simulated, not observed.** Why the simulated yields differ from official statistics, in every case study:
  [FAQ](../about/faq.qmd#why-do-the-simulated-yields-differ-from-the-official-statistics).
- **Uncalibrated.** IR 64 runs with DSSAT's own coefficients, at 105 kg N, without pests, diseases or weeds.
  The yields are above the national average; the comparisons between seasons and regimes are the result.
- **Water at the field.** Irrigation is what the field receives. Canal and pumping losses on the way are not
  counted, and the model has no salt in its water.
- **One flood schedule.** Bund heights, flood depths and their dates come from the 1986 experiment. Other
  water-saving practices, such as letting the field dry between floods, would need another template.
- **Each season starts afresh** at 90% of the soil's available water. In the field the water left at a
  harvest partly carries into the next season; a crop sequence (DSSAT's mode Q, which xdssat runs) would
  follow it.
- **Every rice hectare, both seasons.** MapSPAM gives the physical area of rice; the volumes above assume
  all of it carries both crops.

## Run it yourself

```bash
python scripts/make_templates.py          # writes templates/XDRW8601.RIX
python scripts/prepare_weather.py   --config configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml
python scripts/prepare_crop_mask.py --config configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml
python scripts/prepare_soils.py     --config configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml --aoi mekong_rice
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml --regime irrigated
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml --regime irrigated_perc1
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml --regime irrigated_perc4
python scripts/run_aoi.py --config configs/cases/mekong-rice.yml --regime rainfed
python docs/scripts/export_cases.py mekong
python docs/scripts/export_boundaries.py mekong
```

The three-year version of this area ships with xdssat: `example-inputs/mekong_rice/`
([Examples](../xdssat/examples.qmd)).
